open_points.subject: capture input references
open_points.text: “The functions capability keeps the broad PortRef input contract… Any FileFactsRef… is refused… StoredValuesRef and SpooledFilesRef continue…” None of PortRef, FileFactsRef, StoredValuesRef or SpooledFilesRef is defined, while M23 says NodeExecution names SpooledFiles “by their facts.”
open_points.question: What exact facts distinguish a resolvable SpooledFilesRef from a facts-only FileFactsRef, especially when both originate in a NodeExecution and an empty file list has no element identity?
options: Define a tagged PortRef union with an explicit variant and a resolvable spool identity
Infer the variant from fields present in the reference
Treat every file reference recorded only by facts as FileFactsRef
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicitly tagged union; SpooledFilesRef includes a stable run-spool locator plus checked facts, while FileFactsRef contains facts only.

open_points.subject: captured case inputs
open_points.text: A15 says capture “copies its inputs” from the failed execution, and M06 says “its inputs… become the case's inputs”; the change instead describes a callable receiving and validating a “complete input tuple” of PortRefs.
open_points.question: Must the tuple be derived from the named NodeExecution, must caller-supplied references be proven identical to that execution's recorded inputs, or may the caller choose different readable inputs?
options: Derive the tuple exclusively from the NodeExecution
Accept a supplied tuple only when it exactly matches the NodeExecution inputs
Allow any fitting readable tuple while using the execution only as capture provenance
open_points.default_guess: Derive the tuple exclusively from the NodeExecution and reject any independently supplied replacement inputs.

open_points.subject: capture contract version
open_points.text: The callable “checks [the executed implementation's] contract version against the named version,” but the capture action and M06 do not define a separately named contract-version argument; they derive the case's contract version from the captured execution.
open_points.question: What is the “named version,” how is it supplied or derived, and is an unknown named version handled by A16 as a direct unknown reference before A15 or by this local mismatch check?
options: The request explicitly names a target contract_version_id
The target version is derived from the corpus or slot named by the request
There is no separate target; the execution's implementation determines the version
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit target contract_version_id, resolve it under A16, and then compare it with the resolved implementation's version.

open_points.subject: capture validation precedence
open_points.text: A04 rule 1 says capture failures are checked by port name and, for one port, “presence, carriage, schema, then size”; the change says that after the contract check it checks “the complete input tuple for facts-only file references” before looking up any input value or spooled file, and that “Any FileFactsRef” is refused.
open_points.question: When the tuple is also missing a port, has an extra port, uses the wrong carriage, or otherwise fails an earlier rule-1 fit check, does the global FileFactsRef refusal win, or are tuple presence and structural checks performed first?
options: FileFactsRef scanning precedes every tuple-fit check
Exact port presence is checked first, then FileFactsRef scanning, then carriage/schema/size
All rule-1 fit checks retain precedence over FileFactsRef refusal
open_points.default_guess: Apply the new rule literally: after implementation and contract checks, scan all supplied port references for FileFactsRef before any rule-1 input fit or lookup check.

open_points.subject: capture callable boundary
open_points.text: The new order is said to apply “after… the capture caller's execution and run checks of A15,” so the functions capability relies on another caller having performed the conditions that make an execution capturable.
open_points.question: What prevents another internal caller from invoking the broad capture callable without the A15 execution, failure, sandbox-run and retained-spool checks, and what verifiable evidence tells the callable those checks apply to this exact execution and tuple?
options: Make the callable private to the one capture orchestration path
Pass an unforgeable validated-capture context produced by the A15 checks
Repeat the A15 checks inside the callable
Leave the checks as a caller precondition
open_points.default_guess: Restrict the callable to the capture orchestration path and pass a typed validated context bound to the execution, run and input tuple.
